findings.reason: the plan should extend the catalogue (adding the reverse model→backend index and an unversioned-alias rule) rather than introduce a second home for models in the flight schema.
findings.text: §2 proposes that "the flight schema declares backends with member models" but never cites the model catalogue that already maps every backend to its `model`, `effort`, `alias` and `budget_group`, applied through `reckon/flight.py:1124 _apply_catalogue` and resolved by `reckon/flight.py:185 model_catalogue_path`; the file states it exists precisely so that "choosing a model" is a reckon decision "rather than in a host layer that would make choosing a model a dotfiles commit"

findings.reason: naming the existing predicate makes the exit condition exact and stops a second, drifting definition of "actionable" from being written into the follower.
findings.text: §7's `crew follow --until-actionable` "exits on the first transition that needs the orchestrator" without citing `_needs_you_runs`, which already enumerates exactly the owning session's runs in a needs-the-coordinator state from `recovery.FLEET_BLOCKED_STATES`/`FLEET_UNPROMOTED_STATES`; the plan defines the actionable predicate implicitly

findings.reason: the plan should place the text in the existing contract-composition owner, not in a new per-lane surface.
findings.text: §14 says the recovered per-run advice ("foreground only, no srun, keep calling tools until the manifest is written") "belongs in the worker contract for this lane" without citing the module that composes every worker contract, `reckon/crew/prompts.py` (the named contract constants embedded in every composed prompt) or the §9 digest generator `reckon/crew/worker_digest.py`

findings.reason: the honest shape is one resolver (the catalogue layer) that turns {backend, model, task} into a concrete model/effort, with dispatch merely passing the named value through; as written the decision is spread thin and the plan cannot say which module a reviewer should open.
findings.text: §2 places the model-choice decision across three surfaces it names separately — the flight schema's member-model lists, a new dispatch `--model` flag, and the role/effort overlays in `reckon/crew/routing.py` — and names no module to hide the resolution behind

findings.reason: the plan should extend the existing order (and delete its `sorted(backends)` tail at recovery.py:2055) rather than add a parallel list the ordering function would have to learn to read.
findings.text: §4 introduces an ordered `review_fallback` list as a new mechanism, but `reckon/crew/recovery.py:2031 _ordered_review_lanes` already orders review candidates (owning lane, then local, then the rest) and `_review_excluded_backends` already removes lanes from that order; the plan does not say why the ordered list cannot be expressed by extending that function

findings.reason: a second ordered list forked beside the exclusion list gives two owners of one order, and the plan should name `_ordered_review_lanes` as the function to extend (dropping the alphabetical tail) rather than adding a new config key.
findings.text: §4's `review_fallback` duplicates the ordering owner: review candidate ordering lives in `_ordered_review_lanes` and `_review_lane_candidates`, and the policy that removes a lane already lives in `REVIEW_EXCLUDED_BACKENDS_KEY` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:1994`) declared in `docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml:60`

findings.reason: the lane countermeasures should extend the existing contract constants (and, for the digest route, the canonical policy the digest reads), or the fleet grows a third place the worker rules are written and the three drift.
findings.text: §14 re-asserts the early-turn-ending countermeasures as text for "the worker contract", but the commit-and-manifest-early contract and its siblings are already composed in `reckon/crew/prompts.py` and the §9 work landed `reckon/crew/worker_digest.py` to derive role digests from one canonical policy

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §2 leaves model→backend resolution spread across the flight schema, a new `--model` on dispatch and the role overlays, and names no single module to own the decision.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's member-model tables and §14's lane worker-contract text each fork an owner that already exists (`reckon/flight.py`'s catalogue layer and `reckon/crew/prompts.py`'s contract constants respectively; §4 additionally forks `reckon/crew/recovery.py`'s ordering).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 puts each backend's member models in the flight schema without citing `docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml`, which already declares the model/effort/alias per backend and is documented as "the reckon decision layer for model selection".
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's `review_fallback` is a thin parallel list over the existing ordering mechanism `_ordered_review_lanes` in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`, with no statement of why that mechanism cannot be extended instead.
